answer: Seat every grading committee by age strata: each panel of nine holds at most one key younger than 60 days, two from 60-365 days, and the rest older, drawn by a cipher-seeded beacon nobody can predict. A sybil farm can mint thousands of fresh keys, but age can't be bought, so they fight over one junior chair per panel and never hold a majority. Veteran seats are no relic of privilege either: they rotate every epoch, and the nectar of grading fees is split evenly per seat, not by stake.
